newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees oil price above budget forecast.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees oil price above budget forecast.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday he expected the average oil price to be well above the country's budget forecast of $16.50 per barrel for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

"We hope the oil price will remain stable and maybe it will fall only a little. I think the Indonesian oil price will be a little bit below $20 a barrel," Sudjana told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
Indonesia had set an average price of $16.50 a barrel in its 1996/97 budget.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina has said the government will receive around $600 million for every one dollar increase above the price envisaged in the budget.
But Pertamina says 47 percent of this windfall would be swallowed by the payments for crude to feed its refineries.
Sudjana said OPEC currently produces above its quota ceiling of 25.03 million bpd, but he said global oil supply and demand is almost balanced. Indonesian is OPEC's only Asian members.
Analysts say the group is producing 800,000 bpd above its agreed supply quota of 25.03 million bpd.
